question: A trader lost 5% by selling a shirt for ₹850. He will gain x% by selling it for ₹1,530. The value of x is: 1880
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Selling Prices = Ratio of corresponding Percentages based on CP

SP₁ ÷ (100 − L%) = SP₂ ÷ (100 + P%)

850 ÷ 95 = 1530 ÷ (100 + x)

170 ÷ 19 = 1530 ÷ (100 + x)

100 + x = (1530 × 19) ÷ 170 = 9 × 19 = 171

**∴ The correct answer is x = 71.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price 1 (SP₁) = ₹850, Loss = 5%

Selling Price 2 (SP₂) = ₹1530, Gain = x%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Loss%)

Gain% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 
 SP1 = ₹850 -5% (Loss) CP SP2 = ₹1530 +x% (Gain) 
• 
• 95% (100+x)% CP = 850 × (100 ÷ 95) 

**Calculation:**

⇒ CP = (850 × 100) ÷ (100 − 5)

⇒ CP = 85000 ÷ 95 = ₹17000/19

⇒ Gain = SP₂ − CP = 1530 − 17000/19

⇒ Gain = (29070 − 17000) ÷ 19 = ₹12070/19

⇒ x% = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ x% = [(12070/19) ÷ (17000/19)] × 100

⇒ x% = (12070 ÷ 17000) × 100 = (1207 ÷ 17)% = 71%

⇒ x = 71

**∴ The correct answer is x = 71.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Cost Price Relation

The direct ratio between Marked Price (MP) and Cost Price (CP) when profit and discount percentages are given is: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Successive Profit/Loss Formula

When two successive percentage changes of a% and b% occur, the net effective percentage change is given by: Effective Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Dishonest Dealer Problem

If a trader claims to sell goods at cost price but uses false weights, the profit percentage is always calculated based on the actual weight given: Gain% = [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100.
